passages.text: Paul, an apostle—sent not from men nor by man, but by Jesus Christ and God the Father, who raised Him from the dead— and all the brothers with me, To the churches of Galatia: Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ, who gave Himself for our sins to rescue us from the present evil age, according to the will of our God and Father, to whom be glory forever and ever. Amen.
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle.
God and Jesus Christ sent Paul.
Men did not send Paul.
No human sent Paul.
God is the Father.
God raised Jesus Christ from the dead.
All the brothers with Paul greet you.
Paul writes to the churches in Galatia.
Grace to you from God our Father.
Peace to you from God our Father.
Grace and peace also come from the Lord Jesus Christ.
Jesus Christ gave Himself for our sins.
Jesus Christ did this to rescue us from the present evil age.
God our Father wanted this to happen.
Glory belongs to God our Father forever and ever.
Amen.
passages.original: Παῦλος ἀπόστολος οὐκ ἀπ’ ἀνθρώπων οὐδὲ δι’ ἀνθρώπου ἀλλὰ διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ Θεοῦ Πατρὸς τοῦ ἐγείραντος αὐτὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν καὶ οἱ σὺν ἐμοὶ πάντες ἀδελφοί Ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις τῆς Γαλατίας Χάρις ὑμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη ἀπὸ Θεοῦ Πατρὸς ἡμῶν καὶ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ δόντος ἑαυτὸν ὑπὲρ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ἡμῶν ὅπως ἐξέληται ἡμᾶς ἐκ τοῦ αἰῶνος τοῦ ἐνεστῶτος πονηροῦ κατὰ τὸ θέλημα τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ Πατρὸς ἡμῶν ᾧ ἡ δόξα εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων ἀμήν

passages.text: I am amazed how quickly you are deserting the One who called you by the grace of Christ and are turning to a different gospel— which is not even a gospel. Evidently some people are troubling you and trying to distort the gospel of Christ.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the writer.
Paul is an apostle.
Paul speaks to the churches in Galatia.
Paul says he is amazed.
He sees that the people are leaving the One who called them.
God called them by the grace of Christ.
They are turning to a different gospel.
This different gospel is not really another gospel.
Some people are troubling them.
These people want to change the gospel of Christ.
passages.original: Θαυμάζω ὅτι οὕτως ταχέως μετατίθεσθε ἀπὸ τοῦ καλέσαντος ὑμᾶς ἐν χάριτι Χριστοῦ εἰς ἕτερον εὐαγγέλιον ὃ οὐκ ἔστιν ἄλλο εἰ μή τινές εἰσιν οἱ ταράσσοντες ὑμᾶς καὶ θέλοντες μεταστρέψαι τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τοῦ Χριστοῦ

passages.text: But even if we or an angel from heaven should preach a gospel contrary to the one we preached to you, let him be under a curse!
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle.
Paul speaks with authority from Jesus Christ and God the Father.
Paul addresses the churches in Galatia.
Paul says this to the believers in Galatia.
If we preach a different gospel to you, let us be under a curse.
If an angel from heaven preaches a different gospel to you, let that angel be under a curse.
The gospel we preached to you is the true gospel.
No one should preach a gospel that is different from what you received.
passages.original: Ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐὰν ἡμεῖς ἢ ἄγγελος ἐξ οὐρανοῦ εὐαγγελίζηται ὑμῖν παρ’ ὃ εὐηγγελισάμεθα ὑμῖν ἀνάθεμα ἔστω

passages.text: As we have said before, so now I say again: If anyone is preaching to you a gospel contrary to the one you received, let him be under a curse!
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to the believers in Galatia.
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul has already warned them before.
Paul repeats his warning now.
If anyone preaches a gospel to you that is different from the gospel you received,
let that person be under a curse.
passages.original: ὡς προειρήκαμεν καὶ ἄρτι πάλιν λέγω εἴ τις ὑμᾶς εὐαγγελίζεται παρ’ ὃ παρελάβετε ἀνάθεμα ἔστω

passages.text: Am I now seeking the approval of men, or of God? Or am I striving to please men? If I were still trying to please men, I would not be a servant of Christ.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking.
Paul is a servant of Christ.
Paul asks a question.
Paul asks if he is seeking the approval of people.
Paul asks if he is seeking the approval of God.
Paul asks if he is trying to please people.
Paul says if he were still trying to please people, he would not be a servant of Christ.
passages.original: Ἄρτι γὰρ ἀνθρώπους πείθω ἢ τὸν Θεόν ἢ ζητῶ ἀνθρώποις ἀρέσκειν εἰ ἔτι ἀνθρώποις ἤρεσκον Χριστοῦ δοῦλος οὐκ ἂν ἤμην

passages.text: For I certify to you, brothers, that the gospel I preached was not devised by man.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to the believers.
\r\nPaul calls them brothers.
\r\nPaul says, "I want you to know something."
\r\nPaul preached the gospel to them.
\r\nPaul says, "This gospel did not come from man."
\r\nPaul says, "No human invented this gospel."
passages.original: γνωρίζω γὰρ ὑμῖν ἀδελφοί τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τὸ εὐαγγελισθὲν ὑπ’ ἐμοῦ ὅτι οὐκ ἔστιν κατὰ ἄνθρωπον

passages.text: I did not receive it from any man, nor was I taught it; rather, I received it by revelation from Jesus Christ.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the speaker.
Paul is a servant of Christ.
Paul did not receive the gospel from any man.
No man taught Paul the gospel.
Jesus Christ revealed the gospel to Paul.
passages.original: οὐδὲ γὰρ ἐγὼ παρὰ ἀνθρώπου παρέλαβον αὐτό οὔτε ἐδιδάχθην ἀλλὰ δι’ ἀποκαλύψεως Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ

passages.text: For you have heard of my former way of life in Judaism, how severely I persecuted the church of God and tried to destroy it.
passages.sermon:
I am Paul.
I once lived as a Jew.
You have heard about my former way of life.
I persecuted the church of God very harshly.
I tried to destroy the church.
passages.original: Ἠκούσατε γὰρ τὴν ἐμὴν ἀναστροφήν ποτε ἐν τῷ Ἰουδαϊσμῷ ὅτι καθ’ ὑπερβολὴν ἐδίωκον τὴν ἐκκλησίαν τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ ἐπόρθουν αὐτήν

passages.text: I was advancing in Judaism beyond many of my contemporaries and was extremely zealous for the traditions of my fathers.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the speaker.
Paul practiced Judaism.
Paul advanced in Judaism.
Paul advanced beyond many people his own age.
Paul belonged to the same group as these people.
Paul was extremely zealous.
Paul was zealous for the traditions of his fathers.
passages.original: καὶ προέκοπτον ἐν τῷ Ἰουδαϊσμῷ ὑπὲρ πολλοὺς συνηλικιώτας ἐν τῷ γένει μου περισσοτέρως ζηλωτὴς ὑπάρχων τῶν πατρικῶν μου παραδόσεων

passages.text: But when God, who set me apart from my mother’s womb and called me by His grace, was pleased to reveal His Son in me so that I might preach Him among the Gentiles, I did not rush to consult with flesh and blood, nor did I go up to Jerusalem to the apostles who came before me, but I went into Arabia and later returned to Damascus.
passages.sermon:
God set me apart from birth.
God called me by His grace.
God was pleased to reveal His Son in me.
God did this so I would preach His Son among the Gentiles.
I did not consult with any person right away.
I did not go up to Jerusalem to see the apostles who were before me.
Instead, I went into Arabia.
Then I returned to Damascus.
passages.original: Ὅτε δὲ εὐδόκησεν ὁ θεὸς ὁ ἀφορίσας με ἐκ κοιλίας μητρός μου καὶ καλέσας διὰ τῆς χάριτος αὐτοῦ ἀποκαλύψαι τὸν Υἱὸν αὐτοῦ ἐν ἐμοὶ ἵνα εὐαγγελίζωμαι αὐτὸν ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν εὐθέως οὐ προσανεθέμην σαρκὶ καὶ αἵματι οὐδὲ ἀνῆλθον εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα πρὸς τοὺς πρὸ ἐμοῦ ἀποστόλους ἀλλὰ ἀπῆλθον εἰς Ἀραβίαν καὶ πάλιν ὑπέστρεψα εἰς Δαμασκόν

passages.text: Only after three years did I go up to Jerusalem to confer with Cephas, and I stayed with him fifteen days.
passages.sermon:
I waited three years.
Then I went up to Jerusalem.
I went to meet Cephas.
I stayed with Cephas for fifteen days.
passages.original: Ἔπειτα μετὰ τρία ἔτη ἀνῆλθον εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα ἱστορῆσαι Κηφᾶν καὶ ἐπέμεινα πρὸς αὐτὸν ἡμέρας δεκαπέντε

passages.text: But I saw none of the other apostles except James, the Lord’s brother.
passages.sermon: I did not see any of the other apostles.\r\nI saw only James.\r\nJames is the brother of the Lord.
passages.original: ἕτερον δὲ τῶν ἀποστόλων οὐκ εἶδον εἰ μὴ Ἰάκωβον τὸν ἀδελφὸν τοῦ Κυρίου

passages.text: I assure you before God that what I am writing to you is no lie.
passages.sermon:
Paul wrote this letter to the Galatians.
Paul wanted the Galatians to know the truth.
Paul said, “I am not lying.”
Paul spoke these words before God.
Paul assured them that everything he wrote was true.
passages.original: ἃ δὲ γράφω ὑμῖν ἰδοὺ ἐνώπιον τοῦ Θεοῦ ὅτι οὐ ψεύδομαι

passages.text: Later I went to the regions of Syria and Cilicia.
passages.sermon:
Paul was an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul traveled after meeting James, the Lord’s brother.
Paul went to the regions of Syria.
Paul also went to the regions of Cilicia.
passages.original: Ἔπειτα ἦλθον εἰς τὰ κλίματα τῆς Συρίας καὶ τῆς Κιλικίας

passages.text: I was personally unknown, however, to the churches of Judea that are in Christ.
passages.sermon:
Paul was a follower of Jesus Christ.
The churches of Judea belonged to Christ.
The people in these churches did not know Paul personally.
Paul was unknown to them by face.
passages.original: ἤμην δὲ ἀγνοούμενος τῷ προσώπῳ ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις τῆς Ἰουδαίας ταῖς ἐν Χριστῷ

passages.text: They only heard the account: “The man who formerly persecuted us is now preaching the faith he once tried to destroy.”
passages.sermon:
The churches of Judea are in Christ.
They did not know me personally.
They only heard a report about me.
They heard this: “The man who once persecuted us now preaches the faith.”
He now preaches the faith he once tried to destroy.
passages.original: μόνον δὲ ἀκούοντες ἦσαν ὅτι Ὁ διώκων ἡμᾶς ποτε νῦν εὐαγγελίζεται τὴν πίστιν ἥν ποτε ἐπόρθει

passages.text: And they glorified God because of me.
passages.sermon:
The churches of Judea are in Christ.
They did not know me personally.
They heard about me.
They heard that I once persecuted them.
They heard that I now preach the faith I once tried to destroy.
Because of me, they glorified God.
passages.original: καὶ ἐδόξαζον ἐν ἐμοὶ τὸν Θεόν
